mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (below 4%) and unemployment rate (below 5.0%) signals a strong economic expansion with accommodative monetary policy, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4% AND UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of robust housing construction (HOUST > 2000 thousand units) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars), the economy enters a late-cycle expansion phase that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST > 2000 and RSAFS > 350000, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 100 (2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A non-farm payroll employment level above 130,000 thousand persons indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 200 (1982-1984=100) indicates elevated inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 200, or the Rank IC over any 1-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market boom (HOUST > 2100 thousand units), the construction sector's expansion boosts consumer confidence and spending, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST > 2100, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is < 0.03.
